Integration and integral transforms

Source: vignettes/integration.Rmd
integration.Rmd

symcompR ports SymPy’s integration machinery: a front end, sym_integrate(), that tries several algorithms in turn (table lookup, the rule based integrator that mimics integration by hand, the Risch algorithm, the Risch-Norman heuristic, and integration with Meijer G functions), and the integral transforms built on top of it.

library(symcompR)
x <- Symbol("x"); y <- Symbol("y"); t <- Symbol("t")
s <- Symbol("s"); k <- Symbol("k")
a <- Symbol("a", positive = TRUE); p <- Symbol("p", positive = TRUE)
f <- Function("f")

The function is named sym_integrate() because integrate() already exists in base R (it does numerical integration of R functions).

Indefinite integrals

sym_integrate(e, x) returns an antiderivative, without the constant of integration.

sym_integrate(x^2, x)
#> x^3/3
sym_integrate(1 / x, x)
#> log(x)
sym_integrate(x * cos(x), x)
#> x*sin(x) + cos(x)
sym_integrate(exp(x) * sin(x), x)
#> exp(x)*sin(x)/2 - exp(x)*cos(x)/2
sym_integrate(log(x), x)
#> x*log(x) - x
sym_integrate(tan(x), x)
#> -log(cos(x))
sym_integrate(sin(x)^3, x)
#> cos(x)^3/3 - cos(x)

Rational functions are integrated completely, and algebraic and transcendental integrands are handled by substitution and the Risch machinery.

sym_integrate(1 / (x^2 + 1), x)
#> atan(x)
sym_integrate(1 / (x^3 - 1), x)
#> log(x - 1)/3 - log(x^2 + x + 1)/6 - sqrt(3)*atan(2*sqrt(3)*x/3 + sqrt(3)/3)/3
sym_integrate(sqrt(1 - x^2), x)
#> x*sqrt(1 - x^2)/2 + asin(x)/2
sym_integrate(1 / sqrt(x^2 + 1), x)
#> asinh(x)
sym_integrate(x * exp(-x^2), x)
#> -exp(-x^2)/2

When no elementary antiderivative exists, the answer may involve special functions such as the error function:

sym_integrate(exp(-x^2), x)
#> sqrt(pi)*erf(x)/2

Several variables integrate one after the other:

sym_integrate(x^2 * y, x, y)
#> x^3*y^2/6

Definite and improper integrals

Limits are given as list(x, a, b). Infinite limits use oo.

sym_integrate(x^2, list(x, 0, 1))
#> 1/3
sym_integrate(sin(x), list(x, 0, sym_pi))
#> 2
sym_integrate(abs(x), list(x, -1, 1))
#> 1
sym_integrate(log(x), list(x, 0, 1))
#> -1
sym_integrate(exp(-x), list(x, 0, oo))
#> 1
sym_integrate(1 / x^2, list(x, 1, oo))
#> 1
sym_integrate(1 / (1 + x^2), list(x, -oo, oo))
#> pi
sym_integrate(exp(-x^2), list(x, -oo, oo))
#> sqrt(pi)
sym_integrate(sin(x) / x, list(x, 0, oo))
#> pi/2

Assumptions on parameters matter. With p > 0 the integral defining the gamma function converges, and symcompR recognizes it:

sym_integrate(x^(p - 1) * exp(-x), list(x, 0, oo))
#> gamma(p)
sym_integrate(exp(-p * x), list(x, 0, oo))
#> 1/p

Multiple integrals take one limit list per variable, innermost first.

sym_integrate(x * y, list(x, 0, 1), list(y, 0, 2))
#> 1
sym_integrate(exp(-x^2 - y^2), list(x, -oo, oo), list(y, -oo, oo))
#> pi

An exact result can be evaluated to any precision with N():

I1 <- sym_integrate(exp(-x^2), list(x, 0, 1))
I1
#> sqrt(pi)*erf(1)/2
N(I1, 20)
#> 0.74682413281242702540

Integral objects

Integral() builds an unevaluated integral, which prints, typesets, and evaluates on demand with doit().

J <- Integral(sqrt(x), x)
J
#> Integral(sqrt(x), x)
doit(J)
#> 2*x^(3/2)/3
doit(Integral(x^2, list(x, 0, 3)))
#> 9
latex(Integral(exp(-x^2), list(x, 0, 1)))
#> [1] "\\int\\limits_{0}^{1} e^{- x^{2}}\\, dx"

Individual algorithms

Each integration algorithm can also be called on its own.

manualintegrate() integrates the way a person would, with substitution, integration by parts, and trigonometric rules. integral_steps() returns the tree of rules it applied, which can be used to explain a computation.

manualintegrate(x * sin(x), x)
#> -x*cos(x) + sin(x)
manualintegrate(1 / (x^2 + 2 * x + 5), x)
#> atan(x/2 + 1/2)/2
manualintegrate(exp(x) / (1 + exp(x)), x)
#> log(exp(x) + 1)
integral_steps(x * sin(x), x)
#> PartsRule(integrand=x*sin(x), variable=x, u=x, dv=sin(x), v_step=SinRule(integrand=sin(x), variable=x), second_step=ConstantTimesRule(integrand=-cos(x), variable=x, constant=-1, other=cos(x), substep=CosRule(integrand=cos(x), variable=x)))

risch_integrate() implements the Risch algorithm for elementary functions. It is a decision procedure: when it returns an unevaluated Integral, no elementary antiderivative exists.

risch_integrate(x * exp(x^2), x)
#> exp(x^2)/2
risch_integrate(x * log(x), x)
#> x^2*log(x)/2 - x^2/4
risch_integrate(exp(-x^2), x)
#> Integral(exp(-x^2), x)
risch_integrate(1 / log(x), x)
#> Integral(1/log(x), x)

heurisch() is the Risch-Norman heuristic, ratint() integrates rational functions, and meijerint_indefinite() and meijerint_definite() integrate by converting the integrand to Meijer G functions.

heurisch(x * exp(x), x)
#> x*exp(x) - exp(x)
ratint((x^2 + 1) / (x^2 - 1), x)
#> x + log(x - 1) - log(x + 1)
ratint(1 / (x^2 + 2), x)
#> sqrt(2)*atan(sqrt(2)*x/2)/2
meijerint_indefinite(x * exp(-x), x)
#> -x*exp(-x) - exp(-x)
meijerint_definite(exp(-x^2), x, 0, oo)
#> [[1]]
#> sqrt(pi)/2
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> True

meijerint_definite() returns the value together with the condition under which it holds (here True: no condition).

Lower level entry points: heurisch_wrapper() runs heurisch() and returns a Piecewise that covers the special parameter values, ratint_ratpart() and ratint_logpart() are the rational and logarithmic parts of Horowitz-Ostrogradsky rational integration, meijerint_inversion() inverts a Laplace transform with Meijer G functions, and singularityintegrate() integrates singularity functions.

b <- Symbol("b")
heurisch_wrapper(1 / (x^2 + b), x)
#> Piecewise((log(x - sqrt(-b))/(2*sqrt(-b)) - log(x + sqrt(-b))/(2*sqrt(-b)), Ne(b, 0)), (-1/x, True))
show <- function(l) vapply(l, sstr, "")
show(ratint_ratpart(x + 1, x^3 - 2 * x^2 + x, x))
#> [1] "-2/(x - 1)"   "-1/(x^2 - x)"
show(ratint_logpart(S(1), x^2 - 2, x, t)[[1]])
#> [1] "-4*t + x"  "1 - 8*t^2"
meijerint_inversion(1 / (s^2 + 1), s, t)
#> sin(t)*Heaviside(t)
singularityintegrate(SingularityFunction(x, b, 3), x)
#> SingularityFunction(x, b, 4)/4

Line integrals

line_integrate() integrates along a parametric curve, given as list(t, a, b, x(t), y(t)). Integrating x^2 + y^2 around the unit circle gives its circumference:

line_integrate(x^2 + y^2, list(t, 0, 2 * sym_pi, cos(t), sin(t)), list(x, y))
#> 2*pi
line_integrate(x + y, list(t, 0, 1, t, t^2), list(x, y))
#> -1/12 - asinh(2)/64 + 67*sqrt(5)/96

Laplace transforms

laplace_transform(f, t, s) computes F(s) = \int_0^\infty f(t) e^{-st}\,dt. By default it returns the transform, the abscissa of convergence, and auxiliary conditions; with noconds = TRUE only the transform is returned.

L <- laplace_transform(exp(-a * t), t, s)
L[[1]]
#> 1/(a + s)
L[[2]]
#> -a
laplace_transform(t^2, t, s, noconds = TRUE)
#> 2/s^3
laplace_transform(sin(a * t), t, s, noconds = TRUE)
#> a/(a^2 + s^2)
laplace_transform(t * exp(2 * t), t, s, noconds = TRUE)
#> (s - 2)^(-2)
laplace_transform(Heaviside(t - 3), t, s, noconds = TRUE)
#> exp(-3*s)/s
laplace_transform(DiracDelta(t), t, s, noconds = TRUE)
#> 1

The transform of a derivative brings in the initial value, which is how the Laplace transform turns linear ODEs into algebra:

laplace_transform(diff(f(t), t), t, s, noconds = TRUE)
#> s*LaplaceTransform(f(t), t, s) - f(0)

inverse_laplace_transform() goes back. The Heaviside(t) factor records that the original function is taken to vanish for t < 0.

inverse_laplace_transform(1 / (s^2 + 1), s, t)
#> sin(t)*Heaviside(t)
inverse_laplace_transform(1 / (s * (s + 1)), s, t)
#> Heaviside(t) - exp(-t)*Heaviside(t)
inverse_laplace_transform(1 / (s - 2)^3, s, t)
#> t^2*exp(2*t)*Heaviside(t)/2
inverse_laplace_transform(exp(-2 * s) / s, s, t)
#> Heaviside(t - 2)

LaplaceTransform() is the unevaluated form.

LaplaceTransform(t^2, t, s)
#> LaplaceTransform(t^2, t, s)
doit(LaplaceTransform(t^2, t, s))
#> 2/s^3
InverseLaplaceTransform(1 / s, s, t)
#> InverseLaplaceTransform(1/s, s, t, _None)
doit(InverseLaplaceTransform(1 / s, s, t))
#> Heaviside(t)

laplace_correspondence() replaces unevaluated transforms of known functions by names of their transforms, laplace_initial_conds() inserts initial values, and expand_dirac_delta() writes an expression as a linear combination of Dirac deltas (a constant term and a coefficient for each delta).

Fs <- Function("F")
laplace_correspondence(LaplaceTransform(f(t), t, s), list(list(f, Fs)))
#> F(s)
laplace_initial_conds(s^2 * LaplaceTransform(f(t), t, s) - s * f(0) -
                        subs(diff(f(t), t), t, 0), t, list(list(f, c(2, 4))))
#> s^2*LaplaceTransform(f(t), t, s) - 2*s - 4
ed <- expand_dirac_delta((t^2 + 1) * DiracDelta(t - 1))
ed[[1]]
#> 0
show(ed[[2]][[1]])
#> [1] "DiracDelta(t - 1)" "t^2 + 1"

Fourier, Mellin, sine, cosine, and Hankel transforms

The Fourier transform uses SymPy’s convention F(k) = \int_{-\infty}^\infty f(x) e^{-2\pi i x k}\,dx.

fourier_transform(exp(-x^2), x, k)
#> sqrt(pi)*exp(-pi^2*k^2)
inverse_fourier_transform(sqrt(sym_pi) * exp(-(sym_pi * k)^2), k, x)
#> exp(-x^2)
fourier_transform(exp(-abs(x)), x, k)
#> 2/(4*pi^2*k^2 + 1)

The Mellin transform \int_0^\infty x^{s-1} f(x)\,dx returns the transform and its fundamental strip.

M <- mellin_transform(1 / (1 + x), x, s)
M[[1]]
#> pi/sin(pi*s)
M[[2]]
#> [[1]]
#> 0
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> 1
mellin_transform(exp(-x), x, s, noconds = TRUE)
#> gamma(s)
inverse_mellin_transform(gamma(s), s, x, list(0, oo))
#> exp(-x)

Sine and cosine transforms, and the Hankel transform of order \nu:

sine_transform(exp(-a * x), x, k)
#> sqrt(2)*k/(sqrt(pi)*(a^2 + k^2))
cosine_transform(exp(-a * x), x, k)
#> sqrt(2)*a/(sqrt(pi)*(a^2 + k^2))
inverse_cosine_transform(sqrt(S(2)) * a / (sqrt(sym_pi) * (a^2 + k^2)), k, x)
#> exp(-a*x)
hankel_transform(1 / x, x, k, 0)
#> 1/k
inverse_hankel_transform(1 / k, k, x, 0)
#> 1/x
hankel_transform(exp(-a * x), x, k, 0)
#> a/(k^3*(a^2/k^2 + 1)^(3/2))

Each transform has an unevaluated class as well: FourierTransform(), MellinTransform(), SineTransform(), CosineTransform(), and HankelTransform(), with inverses. Calling doit() on one gives the same result as the matching function above.

FourierTransform(exp(-x^2), x, k)
#> FourierTransform(exp(-x^2), x, k)
InverseFourierTransform(exp(-k^2), k, x)
#> InverseFourierTransform(exp(-k^2), k, x)
doit(SineTransform(exp(-x), x, k))
#> sqrt(2)*k/(sqrt(pi)*(k^2 + 1))
CosineTransform(exp(-x), x, k)
#> CosineTransform(exp(-x), x, k)
InverseSineTransform(1 / k, k, x)
#> InverseSineTransform(1/k, k, x)
InverseCosineTransform(1 / (1 + k^2), k, x)
#> InverseCosineTransform(1/(k^2 + 1), k, x)
MellinTransform(exp(-x), x, k)
#> MellinTransform(exp(-x), x, k)
InverseMellinTransform(gamma(s), s, x, 0, oo)
#> InverseMellinTransform(gamma(s), s, x, 0, oo)
HankelTransform(exp(-x), x, k, 0)
#> HankelTransform(exp(-x), x, k, 0)
InverseHankelTransform(1 / k, k, x, 0)
#> InverseHankelTransform(1/k, k, x, 0)
inverse_sine_transform(sqrt(S(2)) / (sqrt(sym_pi) * k), k, x)
#> 1
